MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: MARINE AND FISHERIES TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 100 °C

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fundamentals of Marine and Freshwater Fisheries? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fundamentals of Marine and Freshwater Fisheries.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fundamentals of Marine and Freshwater Fisheries.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Fundamentals of Marine and Freshwater Fisheries.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fundamentals of Marine and Freshwater Fisheries.

4. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. watt (W)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

5. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

6. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fish Morphology and Anatomy? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Fish Morphology and Anatomy.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Fish Morphology and Anatomy.

   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fish Morphology and Anatomy.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Fundamentals of Capture Fisheries? (1 mark)

   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Fundamentals of Capture Fisheries.

   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Safety and Survival Techniques Page 15 of 34 1 STRAND 1.0: FISH BIOLOGY AND ECOL.

   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only carbon dioxide
